title: How Hotels and Restaurants Get Recommended in AI Answers and Google AI Overviews
seoTitle: How Hotels and Restaurants Show Up in AI Answers
seoDescription: What ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews draw on when they recommend hotels and restaurants, and the parts owners can actually control.
excerpt: AI tools recommend the hotels and restaurants whose facts they can find, read and trust. Most of those facts sit on your website and Google Business Profile.

author: The SocialDM Insights Team
bodyHtml:
Hotels and restaurants get recommended in AI answers when the tools can find clear, consistent and current facts about them in the places they read: your website, your Google Business Profile and what guests write in reviews. Google's AI Overviews are built on its normal search systems, so the same basics decide whether your pages can be cited.

There is no setting you switch on to appear. There is a short list of things owners control, and it is easy to leave a gap in one of them without noticing.

What do AI answers draw on when someone asks for a hotel or restaurant?

They draw on pages they can crawl and index, local business listings and the reviews and descriptions attached to them. Google says a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet to appear as a supporting link in AI Overviews or AI Mode, with no additional technical requirements.

That comes from Google's page on AI features and your website, which also says the usual SEO best practices still apply. For other tools, the rules are their own. OpenAI documents a crawler called OAI-SearchBot that it uses to surface websites in ChatGPT search, and its crawler documentation says sites that block it will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers, though they can still appear as plain navigational links. Blocking GPTBot, which relates to model training, is a separate choice.

Here is how I sort the inputs for a hospitality business:

SourceWhat it tells an AI toolWho controls it
Your websiteRooms, rates policy, menus, hours, location, events, policiesYou
Google Business ProfileCategory, hours, amenities, menu, photos, booking linksYou, once verified
Guest reviewsWhat people actually liked or did notGuests, though you can earn and answer them
Press, guides and local sitesWhether others consider you worth mentioningPartly you, through real stories worth covering

What can a hotel or restaurant owner actually control?

You control the accuracy of your own website, the completeness of your Business Profile, how you ask for and answer reviews, and whether your site lets AI crawlers in. You do not control which sources a tool chooses for a given question.

I keep that split in front of clients, because it stops a lot of wasted effort. Nobody can promise placement in an AI answer, and anyone who does is guessing. What you can do is remove the reasons a tool would skip you or get you wrong.

Why does your website still matter if guests never click?

Because your website is where AI tools find the facts they repeat. If your menu, room types, pet policy, parking or private dining details live only in an image, a PDF or a booking widget, a tool may not be able to read them, and it will fill the gap from somewhere else.

Things I check first on a hotel or restaurant site:

  • Menus as text. A photo of a menu is fine for guests, but put the dishes, dietary notes and price ranges on a normal page too.
  • One page per thing people ask about. Private events, brunch, the patio, the pool, accessible rooms. A clear page with a plain heading answers a question an AI tool is trying to answer.
  • The same facts everywhere. Hours, address, phone and check in times should match across the site, your profile and the major listing sites.
  • Pages that are indexed. Check Search Console. A page Google has not indexed cannot be a supporting link.
  • Structured data that matches the page. Google's AI features guidance says structured data should match the visible text. Markup that claims something the page does not say is a problem, not a shortcut.
  • Robots rules you chose on purpose. Look at your robots.txt with whoever runs the site, and decide deliberately whether to allow OAI-SearchBot and similar search crawlers.

How much does the Google Business Profile matter for AI answers?

For Google, a great deal, because the profile is the structured record of your hours, category, amenities, menu and reviews. Google says local results are based primarily on relevance, distance and prominence, and it defines relevance as how well a profile matches what someone is searching for.

That is from Google's page on how to improve your local ranking. Google has not published a separate rulebook for how local businesses are chosen inside AI Overviews, so I treat the profile and the website as the two inputs that carry most of the weight you can influence. For restaurants, Google's help page on menus lets you build a menu in the profile or link to one on your site. For hotels, Google's hotel Business Profile guide explains how to edit amenities once the profile is verified. Both are easy to leave half finished.

Do reviews influence whether AI recommends you?

Google says more reviews and positive ratings can improve local ranking, so for Google they matter directly. For other AI tools, reviews are public text that often describes exactly what a guest wants to know, like whether the rooftop is loud or the kitchen handles allergies well.

I would not chase a star number. I would ask every happy guest for a review in plain words, reply to reviews with specifics, and fix the operational issue behind a repeated complaint. A recurring complaint tends to keep showing up in what guests read, whatever you post.

How do you check what AI tools say about your property today?

Ask the questions your guests ask, in the tools they use, and write down the answers with the date. Try ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and a Google search that shows an AI Overview, and use unbranded questions such as "boutique hotel near the convention center with parking" or "quiet restaurant for a business dinner in Old Town."

Note whether you appear, what is said, and whether it is correct. Then trace any error to its likely source. Common culprits are an old menu, a stale listing or a detail that only exists in a review. Repeat the check monthly, since answers shift.

This is the search and AI readiness work we do on our hospitality marketing engagements, alongside story led social and Google Business Profile management.

Questions we hear

Can a hotel or restaurant pay to be recommended in AI Overviews?

No. Google says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. What you can do is make your website and Business Profile accurate, complete and easy to read.

Does ChatGPT use our Google Business Profile?

OpenAI has not said how ChatGPT uses Business Profiles. What it does document is OAI-SearchBot, the crawler used to surface websites in ChatGPT search, so your own website needs to be readable to it.

Do we need special schema or an AI file to show up?

Google says there are no extra technical requirements for its AI features beyond being indexed and eligible for a snippet. Structured data still helps search engines understand a page, as long as it matches what the page actually says.

Why does AI give the wrong hours or prices for our restaurant?

Usually because the source it read is out of date or inconsistent, such as an old PDF menu or a listing nobody updated. Fix the facts at the source and keep them the same everywhere.

How do we check what AI tools say about us?

Ask the questions a guest would ask, in several tools, from the area guests search from, and write down the answers with the date. Repeat it monthly, because answers change.

sources.claim: Page must be indexed and eligible for a snippet to be a supporting link in AI Overviews or AI Mode; no additional technical requirements; SEO best practices apply; structured data should match visible text
OAI-SearchBot surfaces websites in ChatGPT search; sites that opt out are not shown in ChatGPT search answers but may appear as navigational links; GPTBot is separate
Local results based primarily on relevance, distance and prominence; relevance defined; more reviews and positive ratings can improve local ranking; no way to pay for better local ranking
Restaurants can add a menu or a menu link to the Business Profile
Hotels can edit amenities on a verified Business Profile

takeaways: Google says a page must be indexed and eligible for a snippet to appear as a supporting link in AI Overviews, with no extra technical requirements.
Hotels and restaurants should publish menus, amenities and policies as readable text on their own websites, not only in images, PDFs or booking widgets.
OpenAI says sites that block its OAI-SearchBot crawler will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers.
Nobody can promise placement in an AI answer, but accurate profiles, consistent facts and real reviews remove the reasons a tool would skip you.
